discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, founding moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electron bands nearly flat, so that interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this with remarkably clean experiments. They found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity, tunable by a gate voltage, in a material made only of carbon. Many groups worldwide quickly reproduced these results. The work created a new field: the twist angle became a control parameter for quantum matter. This led to moiré platforms in graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenides showing orbital magnetism, Wigner crystals, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and, most recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. Few discoveries in recent condensed-matter physics have opened so much new physics to so many groups. The close interplay between a simple theoretical prediction and a decisive experiment is exemplary.
